title: chant run event
description: One event of a run's stream (#4019, behold #678): one JSON object per line, written by writeRunEvent and createRunEventWriter in src/run-event.ts. It covers Op runs, component runs and pipeline runs alike. Every event names the run, what it ran, the commit it built from and the runtime it ran on, so a reader shows a run the same way wherever it happened. A run's stream opens with run-start and ends with run-settle, whose status is the run's verdict; seq counts the events from 0. Version 1 of the read contract. Readers ignore fields they do not know; a field is only ever added within a version. A status set gains a value only as an addition within a version, which the read contract lists with the chant that first writes it; a reader treats a status it does not know as a settle it cannot classify and reads on. Contract version 1 of this document is written by chant 0.124.28 and newer; the read contract as a whole by chant 0.81.0 and newer.

chant.description: The version of the chant that wrote the event.

seq.description: The event's place in its run's stream: 0 for run-start, one more for each event after it.

runId.description: The run's own id: an Op run's id, a component run's id (the id its release records carry, the CI run id in CI, else one minted locally), or the CI run id for a pipeline run. runOrigin says where it ran, which for an Op run in CI is the CI run, not the id space of runId.

kind.description: What ran: an Op, a component selection (chant run --components), or a CI pipeline.

name.description: The Op's name, the component selection as given, or the pipeline's name.

gitSha.description: The commit the run built from, the same field a release record carries. Null when the run did not start in a git checkout.

runtime.description: Where the run happened: in the process that started it, on a steward, or in a forge's CI.

runOrigin.description: Where the run ran and how to reach it: RunOrigin from lifecycle/release-ledger.ts, the shape a release record's runOrigin has. For an Op run in CI it locates the CI run, as the Op's run record does (#4020), while runId stays the Op run's own id.

forge.description: github: a GitHub Actions run, also the spelling Forgejo Actions uses. gitlab: a CI pipeline. op: a steward's run, named by its Op run id. local: a run on the machine that started it, outside CI. chant: a pull-request job the chant runner ran (chant ci run, #4094), named by its Op run id; added within contract version 1 and written by chant 0.124.30 and newer, so a reader that switches on forge keeps a case for a value it does not know.

repo.description: The repository or project slug on the forge, when the environment named one.

url.description: A link to the run, when the environment gave enough to build one.

jobId.description: The forge's id for the job within the run: GITHUB_JOB on GitHub and Forgejo, CI_JOB_ID on GitLab. Added within contract 1 by #4156 and written by chant 0.124.32 and newer, only by chant ci run in a forge job.

attempt.description: The run's attempt, GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT on GitHub and Forgejo. Added within contract 1 by #4156 and written by chant 0.124.32 and newer, only by chant ci run in a forge job.

settleStatus.description: How a run, wave, component or phase settled. gated: it stopped at a gate nobody has approved. waiting: it stopped at a decision point nobody has answered. Neither is a failure.

stepIndex.description: The step's place in its phase as authored, counting from 0, so two steps of one phase that share a name stay apart. Optional, added within contract 1 by chant 0.124.28 (#4041). A writer leaves it out for a step it has no authored place for, and a reader without it pairs a step-start with its step-settle by component, phase and step in stream order.

component.description: The component whose composition the phase or step belongs to in a component run, and null in an Op or pipeline run.

allOf.description: The run is about to start.

waves.description: In a component run, the waves of components the run will attempt, in order; wave numbers in later events count from 1 into this list. Null in an Op or pipeline run.

allOf.description: The run settled. The last event of the stream, and its verdict.

durationMs.description: From run-start to now, or null when the writer did not time it.

error.description: With status failed, what failed, when the writer knows.

failure.description: Added within contract version 1 by #4094, written by chant 0.124.30 and newer. With status failed: why, as the run record's failure says. code is a pull-request report's refusal or status (not-approved, plan-changed, not-a-reviewer, no-pull-request, plan-failed, failed, refused) or command-failed, setup-failed or build-failed, and a reader keeps a case for a code it does not know. reason is one line for a person, phase the phase that failed, exitCode the failed command's exit code. chant ci run writes it on every failed job.

allOf.description: A wave of a component run is about to start. Its components may run at the same time.
A wave settled. failed if any component in it failed, which stops the run before the next wave.
A component in a wave is about to start its deploy composition.

A component's composition settled, after any rollback the run did for it. A component the run did not start settles too, with no component-start before it: blocked when a dependency failed or stopped at a gate, already-applied when an earlier attempt the run resumed applied it.

status.description: The settle statuses of a run, wave or phase, and two more for a component the run did not start, added within contract version 1 by #4007 and written by chant 0.124.29 and newer. blocked: a dependency failed or stopped at a gate, so it never ran; blockedBy names the dependency. already-applied: an earlier attempt the run resumed applied it, so it did not run again; its wave is the wave it had in that attempt's derivation. A reader that knows only the four settle statuses can read either as a component that did not run in this run.

blockedBy.description: With blocked: the failed or gated component the run reached this one from. Added within contract version 1 by #4007, written by chant 0.124.29 and newer.

allOf.description: A phase is about to run its steps: an Op's phase, a component composition's phase, or a pipeline's stage.
A phase settled: ok when every step in it settled ok, skipped or cached.
A step is about to run: an Op or composition step, or a pipeline's job. A step that never started, such as one an earlier failure stopped, has a step-settle and no step-start.

step.description: The step's activity, gate:<name> for a gate, effect:<name> for an effect, or the job's name.

status.description: ok: it ran and succeeded. failed: it ran and failed. skipped: it did not run, and skip says why. cached: a cache hit stood in for running it (#4015). gated: it stopped the run at a gate nobody has approved. waiting: it stopped the run at a decision point nobody has answered.

skip.description: With status skipped. receipt: the effect's receipt matched, so it had already applied. resumed: the run resumed at a later gate and carried this step's output from an earlier run. refused: it declined to go on, and message says why. not-run: an earlier step failed or stopped the run. Null when the writer does not know.

durationMs.description: How long it ran, or null when the writer did not time it.

message.description: Why a step skipped, gated or waited, for a person.

resources.description: Added within contract version 1 by #4615, written by chant 0.124.55 and newer. What the step did to each resource, when its engine reported it, such as plunge's per-resource timings on a pulumi-up step. A reader that does not know it ignores it.

resource.description: The engine's id for it: a URN, an address.

allOf.description: The run stopped and waits on a person: a gate nobody has approved, or a decision point nobody has answered. The step settles gated or waiting next.

op.description: The op the gate is recorded under, which chant approve takes. It differs from name when a step's command stopped at a gate of its own.

gate.description: The gate's name, or null when the step waits on a decision point alone.

point.description: The answer record id of the open question, which points answer takes, or null.

message.description: Why the gate did not pass, such as an approval for a different plan.

allOf.description: A gate the run reached was approved, so its step goes on.

resolvedAt.description: When the approval was recorded, ISO-8601.

via.description: How the approval passed when it was more than one person's approval of this gate: a quorum, a policy permit, a decision point's answer, or an approval recorded under one of the gate's aliases. empty (added within contract 1 by #4045, chant 0.124.28 and newer): a release gate passed over an empty change set with no approval, on the resolution the promote wrote, whose resolvedBy is the actor running it. workspace (added within contract 1 by #2554, chant 0.124.47 and newer): a workspace gate's approval stood in for this member gate, because the member opts in at base and the approval covers this plan.

url.description: Where the approval was made, when known.
